title: Satisfaction
summary: A semantic relation stating that a formula holds in a declared interpretation or model.

context.note: The exact satisfaction relation depends on the language and semantic framework.

assumptions.text: A language, an interpretation/model M, and a formula P suitable for that semantics are fixed.

content.plain: A formula can be true in one mathematical structure and false in another. QEVA must name the semantics or model when it uses semantic truth.
content.exact: The notation M |= P denotes that P is satisfied by model M according to the declared semantic clauses for the language in use.
content.example: A sentence about order can hold in one ordered structure and fail in another.
content.caveat: The symbol |= has framework-specific semantics. A QEVA record must not silently identify semantic truth with formal provability.

relations.note: Satisfaction is semantic; derivability is syntactic.

verification.method: QEVA seed formulation checked editorially for mathematical coherence; no external formal proof artifact is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA seed archive
provenance.source_note: Seed record written to make QEVA Protocol 0.2 explicit. It is an editorial mathematical formulation, not a claim that one foundation is uniquely privileged.
